provenance.coverage: Original Terminal-Bench 2.0 test suite (8 tests) and Harbor reward.
provenance.derivation: Converted by anchors_convert.py from Terminal-Bench 2.0 'nginx-request-logging' at https://github.com/laude-institute/terminal-bench-2.git@69671fbaac6d67a7ef0dfec016cc38a64ef7a77c (task tree_sha256 31ddf4ecf2e7ce9888d5ac04ddf99ac2e54861a11e18a37fe29fdd1991768fb3, git tree 7fb41899fff6ce5e3ccb43d562d441ee1b9b2e20), image alexgshaw/nginx-request-logging@sha256:693e64431a0dbf45952e8b91a298d54fd60247e501c6623fb8fa3ebc07fc3d3d. Base = the untouched bounded workspace; reference = the declared artifacts after running the task's own solution/solve.sh in the task image; hidden checks = the original tests/ run unmodified by test.sh, one strict row per test ID plus the Harbor reward row. Adaptation: step 1 of the instruction (install Nginx) needs network, so the solution's own 'apt-get update && apt-get install -y nginx' is hoisted into the environment image. test_nginx_installed therefore passes for the base too; every other test still fails at base. Adaptation: the native agent cannot start services; the trusted verifier runs the declared start command 'nginx' after materializing the artifacts (instruction steps 7-9 are performed or observed by the verifier). sites-enabled/default is a symlink in the image; it is exported as a regular file with the target's content. Writing it empty disables the default site (the file is then absent). Docker containers have IPv6 disabled (as in Harbor's default docker environment), so the stock default site's 'listen [::]:80' fails 'nginx -t'; that is why the base also fails test_nginx_config_syntax.
provenance.historical_exposure: Public benchmark (Terminal-Bench 2.0, with its training-corpora canary); likely seen in training data. Reported separately, never pooled.
provenance.limitations: No model trial, representative-day coverage, native isolation, or contamination-free claim.
